title: A Unified Solution to Diverse Heterogeneities in One-Shot Federated Learning

problem.claim: One-Shot Federated Learning limits communication to a single server-client round, but existing frameworks remain vulnerable to distributional heterogeneity.

gap.claim: Existing OSFL frameworks primarily address model heterogeneity while neglecting data heterogeneity.

contributions.claim: FedHydra is a unified, data-free OSFL framework designed to address both model and data heterogeneity.
FedHydra uses model stratification and heterogeneity-aware stratified aggregation in a two-stage learning mechanism.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly distinguish FedHydra's two-stage learning mechanism as novel relative to existing OSFL approaches.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors compared FedHydra with five state-of-the-art baselines on four benchmark datasets.
The authors report that FedHydra outperforms previous OSFL methods in homogeneous and heterogeneous settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: OSFL reduces communication and privacy-leakage risks by restricting communication to one round.
Existing OSFL frameworks focus on model heterogeneity and neglect data heterogeneity.
FedHydra is proposed as a unified data-free framework for both heterogeneity types.
The framework uses a novel two-stage mechanism with model stratification and heterogeneity-aware stratified aggregation.
The authors report comparisons against five baselines across four datasets and improved performance in both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings.

source_observation.claim: The framework monitors data and model heterogeneity from different aspects during learning.

interpretation.claim: Separating heterogeneity-aware mechanisms may help manage conflicts between distinct sources of variation.

application.claim: In constrained federated settings, consider jointly modeling client-model and client-data differences rather than optimizing for only one.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported OSFL settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, evaluation metrics, quantitative results, or statistical variation.
The abstract does not describe the baselines, experimental protocol, or privacy-leakage evaluation.
